newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on late buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended slightly up on Wednesday due to late buying by individuals for long-term investment, brokers said.
The B share index inched up 0.16 point, or 0.18 percent, to 89.71 on turnover of HK$20.79 million, compared with HK$15.81 million on Tuesday.
Despite a weekend ban on Chinese buying new B shares, domestic investors were unwilling to liquidate their positions at current levels, a broker at China Southern Securities said.
Investors seem to have reached a consensus that the market has a limited downside and plenty of room to rise in future, the broker said.
The B share index is likely to fluctuate in a narrow band and in light trading later this week ahead of a three-day National Day holiday, brokers said.
There will be no stock trading in Shenzhen and Shanghai from September 30 to October 2 because of the holiday. Trading will resume on October 3.
The index should meet strong support at the 86-point level over the short term, with resistance seen at the 90-point level, a second broker said.
China Bicycle was the star, up HK$0.08, or 4.44 percent, to HK$1.88 on the day's second heaviest trade of 988,051 shares.
But a company spokesman said on Wednesday that the firm has lowered its 1996 sales target to 1.20 million bicycles from an original 1.80 million.
Property concenn Vanke followed, rising HK$0.15, or 3.45 percent, to HK$4.50. Shenzhen International Enterprise jumped HK$0.06 to HK$2.68 and Gintian rose HK$0.05 to HK$2.35.

Driven by profit-taking, the A share index shed 1.35 points, or 0.49 percent, to 271.89 on turnover of 4.61 billion yuan, up from Tuesday's 4.17 billion, brokers said. The composite index fell 1.16 points, or 0.45 percent, to 257.11.
Textile issue Shenzhen Huaxin was hit by profit-taking and fell 0.39 yuan, or 5.56 percent, to 6.62 yuan.
Baoshi Electronic, which listed 26.20 million class A shares and 3.7779 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Wednesday, ended the session at 10.45 yuan on trade of 20.05 million shares.
